title: OptoMMP: Added expanded memory ranges and descriptions.
description:
Added the expanded ranges of memory addresses and their descriptions as listed in Chapter 4 of [Opto 22's Document on the OptoMMP Protocol](https://documents.opto22.com/1465_OptoMMP_Protocol_Guide.pdf).

Took out the TCP/UDP heuristic method additions from the original merge request in order to push simpler changes until I can the Linux test suite passing on my end.

Thank you for the tip, @AndersBroman. Admittedly, I'm new to contributing to open source projects of Wireshark's size. The commit checks are passing now. And I've selected the option to squash commit messages on merge. I'm not seeing how to squash any messages before that, as it seems the tree nodes don't meet the requirements to squash. But I could be wrong. For what it's worth, all this history you're seeing has been my mangled attempt to get one small change done to one file.

Unfortunately the squash commits on merge doesn't really work well, it's way better for you to squash your MR first.

Incidentally doing so makes (IMHO) reviewing your changes much easier as I have one commit to look at.

I also think you have two separate changes now, the memory ranges and descriptions and the TCP\UDP heuristics, so they should probably be 2 separate MR's.

I can see how the squashed commits before the merge would make your job easier. For the life of me, I would love to do that if I could see a way to. With the rebasing I've been doing to stay current with the main Wireshark branch, I see no direct children commits I could squash.

You're correct. My initial MR included the TCP/UDP heuristics. I removed those from this MR. Now the only change is the added memory ranges and descriptions.

Do you have any suggestions for how I should proceed? Should I cancel this MR, and make a new MR with just the one change I'm targeting?
